units.title: Una nueva clase
units.objective: Encontrar nombre, lugar y un objeto en un mensaje breve.
units.strategy: Busca nombres y números. Lee una oración cada vez; no necesitas traducir todo.
units.passage: Hello! My name is Eva. I am a student. My English class is in room six. My teacher is Ben. I have a blue notebook and a black pen. The class starts at nine. I sit next to Ana. She is a new student too.

questions.prompt: Who is the teacher?
options: Ben
Eva
Ana
Leo
questions.explanation: El texto identifica a Ben como profesor.
questions.evidence: My teacher is Ben.

questions.prompt: Where is the class?
options: In room nine
In room six
In room two
In room ten
questions.explanation: Six indica el aula; nine indica la hora.
questions.evidence: My English class is in room six.

questions.prompt: What is this message about?
options: Ben and his family
Ana and her job
Eva and her English class
Eva and her lunch
questions.explanation: Eva se presenta y describe su clase, sus útiles y una compañera.
questions.evidence: My name is Eva. I am a student. My English class is in room six.

units.title: Un pedido sencillo
units.objective: Reconocer productos y quién los consume.
units.strategy: Une cada nombre con su pedido. Fíjate en not: cambia la información.
units.passage: I am at a cafe with my brother Tom. I want a sandwich and a glass of water. Tom wants soup and tea. The soup is hot. We sit at a small table near the door. I do not want tea today.

questions.prompt: What does the writer want to drink?
options: Tea
Water
Coffee
Milk
questions.explanation: El narrador pide agua y aclara que no quiere té.
questions.evidence: I want a sandwich and a glass of water.

questions.prompt: Who wants soup?
options: The writer
The teacher
Tom
The cook
questions.explanation: La frase asigna sopa y té a Tom.
questions.evidence: Tom wants soup and tea.

questions.prompt: What is the text mainly about?
options: Two people cooking at home
A person buying a table
A person looking for a door
Two people ordering food
questions.explanation: Describe lo que dos personas desean comer en un café.
questions.evidence: I am at a cafe with my brother Tom. I want a sandwich and a glass of water. Tom wants soup and tea.

units.title: Un aviso del autobús
units.objective: Distinguir horario habitual y cambio puntual.
units.strategy: Compara usually con today. No mezcles el horario habitual con el cambio.
units.passage: The number eight bus usually stops outside the library. Today the road is closed, so the bus stops near the park. The first bus is at seven and the last bus is at nine in the evening. Please buy your ticket from the driver. The ticket price is the same today.

questions.prompt: Where does the bus stop today?
options: Outside the library
At the station
Near the park
Behind the school
questions.explanation: Today introduce el lugar temporal.
questions.evidence: Today the road is closed, so the bus stops near the park.

questions.prompt: Does the ticket cost more today?
options: Yes, it costs twice as much
No, tickets are free
Yes, only evening tickets cost more
No, the price is unchanged
questions.explanation: Same significa que el precio no cambia.
questions.evidence: The ticket price is the same today.

questions.prompt: Why is this notice useful?
options: It tells passengers about a different stop
It explains how to become a driver
It announces a new library
It advertises a cheaper ticket
questions.explanation: El aviso informa del cambio de parada por cierre de la vía.
questions.evidence: Today the road is closed, so the bus stops near the park.

units.title: La cocina compartida
units.objective: Relacionar una norma con su propósito explícito.

vocabulary.example: The bowl is on the shelf.
The milk is in the fridge.

units.strategy: Busca please y after para reconocer instrucciones y su orden.
units.passage: Welcome to our shared kitchen. Please wash your cup after breakfast. Put clean plates on the shelf, not on the table. Write your name on your food in the fridge. This helps everyone find the right lunch. We clean the floor on Friday. You can use the kitchen every day.

questions.prompt: Where do clean plates go?
options: On the floor
In the fridge
On the table
On the shelf
questions.explanation: La instrucción contrasta shelf con table.
questions.evidence: Put clean plates on the shelf, not on the table.

questions.prompt: Why should people write their names on food?
options: To find their own lunch
To choose a cleaning day
To ask for breakfast
To buy new plates
questions.explanation: El propósito se explica inmediatamente después de la norma.
questions.evidence: This helps everyone find the right lunch.

questions.prompt: When can people use the kitchen?
options: Only on Friday
Every day
Only after breakfast
Only at lunch
questions.explanation: El viernes corresponde a limpieza del suelo, no al único día de uso.
questions.evidence: You can use the kitchen every day.

units.title: Cambio de planes
units.objective: Seguir una secuencia en pasado y explicar una decisión.
units.strategy: Marca first, when y instead si aparecen. Distingue el plan inicial del resultado.
units.passage: On Saturday, Luis went to the market to buy tomatoes for dinner. He took a basket because he did not want a plastic bag. When he arrived, the tomato stall was empty. The seller suggested carrots instead. Luis bought some and made carrot soup at home. His original plan changed, but his family enjoyed the meal.

questions.prompt: What did Luis originally want to buy?
options: Tomatoes
Carrots
Soup
Plastic bags
questions.explanation: El plan inicial se da en la primera oración.
questions.evidence: Luis went to the market to buy tomatoes for dinner.

questions.prompt: Why did he take a basket?
options: To give it to the seller
To avoid using a plastic bag
To carry cooked soup
To collect a gift
questions.explanation: Because introduce la razón explícita.
questions.evidence: He took a basket because he did not want a plastic bag.

questions.prompt: Which summary fits the story?
options: Luis returned without any food
Luis bought everything he first planned
Luis changed his dinner plan successfully
Luis cooked a meal nobody liked
questions.explanation: No consiguió tomates, compró zanahorias y su familia disfrutó el resultado.
questions.evidence: His original plan changed, but his family enjoyed the meal.

units.title: Una invitación al club
units.objective: Identificar requisitos y aclaraciones en una invitación.
units.strategy: Distingue lo obligatorio de lo opcional: need y do not need.
units.passage: Our walking club meets at the station on Sunday at ten. We will walk to the lake and have lunch there. Bring comfortable shoes and a bottle of water. You do not need to bring food because the club will provide sandwiches. If it rains, we will meet inside the station and choose a shorter route.

questions.prompt: What will the club provide?
options: Shoes
Sandwiches
Water bottles
Train tickets
questions.explanation: La comida la proporciona el club.
questions.evidence: the club will provide sandwiches.

questions.prompt: What changes if it rains?
options: The meeting moves to Saturday
Everyone must bring lunch
The group chooses a shorter route
The group meets at the lake
questions.explanation: La condición modifica la ruta y el lugar exacto de encuentro en la estación.
questions.evidence: If it rains, we will meet inside the station and choose a shorter route.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the message?
options: To sell shoes at the station
To describe a past holiday
To explain how to swim in a lake
To help people prepare for a walk
questions.explanation: Incluye hora, lugar, material y alternativa por lluvia.
questions.evidence: Bring comfortable shoes and a bottle of water.

units.title: Una solicitud de trabajo
units.objective: Comparar dos espacios según una necesidad concreta.
units.strategy: Busca however y because. Evalúa la necesidad de la persona, no tu preferencia.
units.passage: Nora works from home twice a week, but her flat is noisy in the mornings. She asked a nearby study centre about its desks. The shared room is cheaper and allows phone calls. The quiet room costs more, but calls are not allowed. Nora needs to read reports without interruptions, so she booked the quiet room for Tuesday morning.

questions.prompt: Which room allows phone calls?
options: The quiet room
Both rooms
The shared room
Neither room
questions.explanation: La política se especifica para el espacio compartido.
questions.evidence: The shared room is cheaper and allows phone calls.

questions.prompt: Why did Nora choose the quiet room?
options: She wants to make several calls
It is the cheaper option
Her flat is far from the centre
She needs to read without interruptions
questions.explanation: Su prioridad es concentrarse, no ahorrar ni llamar.
questions.evidence: Nora needs to read reports without interruptions, so she booked the quiet room for Tuesday morning.

questions.prompt: What can we infer about Nora’s choice?
options: She accepted a higher price for a quieter space
She believed both rooms cost the same
She planned to ignore the rule about calls
She stopped working from home completely
questions.explanation: El cuarto elegido cuesta más y responde a su necesidad de silencio.
questions.evidence: The quiet room costs more, but calls are not allowed.

units.title: Una reparación con condiciones
units.objective: Interpretar plazo, condición y acción solicitada.

vocabulary.example: Leave now; otherwise, you will be late.
You can collect your bag here.

units.strategy: Separa lo confirmado de lo condicional: if no es una promesa.
units.passage: Dear Alex, we have checked your bicycle. The brakes need new parts, but the tyres are fine. We can finish the repair on Thursday if the parts arrive tomorrow. Otherwise, it will be ready on Friday. Please reply before five today to confirm the repair. We will send another message when you can collect the bicycle.

questions.prompt: What needs replacing?
options: The tyres
The seat
The whole bicycle
Parts of the brakes
questions.explanation: El mensaje distingue los frenos de los neumáticos, que están bien.
questions.evidence: The brakes need new parts, but the tyres are fine.

questions.prompt: What must Alex do before five?
options: Confirm the repair by replying
Collect the bicycle
Order the parts himself
Bring the bicycle to the shop
questions.explanation: El plazo se refiere a responder, no a recoger.
questions.evidence: Please reply before five today to confirm the repair.

questions.prompt: Is Thursday a guaranteed collection day?
options: Yes, the repair is already complete
No, completion depends on the parts arriving
Yes, because the tyres are fine
No, the shop is closed on Thursdays
questions.explanation: If expresa una condición pendiente; también debe esperar el aviso de recogida.
questions.evidence: We can finish the repair on Thursday if the parts arrive tomorrow.

units.title: Un jardín que se adapta
units.objective: Reconocer problema, intervención y resultado en una narración.

vocabulary.example: Finishing the project was an achievement.

units.strategy: Lee primero para identificar el problema general; después busca pruebas del cambio.
units.passage: When our neighbourhood opened a community garden, volunteers planted vegetables in long rows. After the first month, they noticed that older visitors rarely joined the work. A short survey revealed that bending down was difficult for some people. The group used donated wood to build raised beds beside a wide path. More visitors began helping with the plants, although the garden did not become larger. The coordinator says the main achievement was not growing extra vegetables. It was giving more neighbours a practical way to take part. Next spring, the group plans to add labels in larger print.

questions.prompt: What difficulty did the survey identify?
options: Bending down was difficult for some visitors
The garden was too far away
Visitors disliked all vegetables
There were too many signs
questions.explanation: La encuesta identifica una barrera física específica.
questions.evidence: A short survey revealed that bending down was difficult for some people.

questions.prompt: What was the coordinator’s main achievement?
options: Producing the largest possible harvest
Making participation easier for more neighbours
Expanding the size of the garden
Reducing the number of volunteers
questions.explanation: El coordinador contrasta producción con participación.
questions.evidence: It was giving more neighbours a practical way to take part.

questions.prompt: Why are larger labels a logical next step?
options: They would replace the raised beds
They would increase the garden’s land area
They could remove another barrier to participation
They would stop neighbours asking questions
questions.explanation: Ya se adapta el jardín a sus usuarios; letras mayores facilitan leer. No se promete un resultado medido.
questions.evidence: Next spring, the group plans to add labels in larger print.

units.title: Una reseña equilibrada
units.objective: Distinguir valoración general y recomendación condicionada.
units.strategy: No decidas el tono por una sola palabra. Compara elogios, problemas y conclusión.
units.passage: I spent two nights at the Harbour Guesthouse while attending a course. The room was small but clean, and the host left breakfast ready before my early bus. Unfortunately, music from the cafe below continued until eleven on Saturday. I mentioned this the next morning, and the host offered me a room at the back for my second night. That room was much quieter. I would stay again for a short work trip, but I would request a back room when booking. Travellers who need silence every evening should ask about local events before they decide.

questions.prompt: What did the host do after the complaint?
options: Cancelled the course
Offered a room at the back
Closed the cafe
Changed the bus time
questions.explanation: La respuesta concreta fue cambiar de habitación.
questions.evidence: the host offered me a room at the back for my second night.

questions.prompt: How would the writer describe the stay overall?
options: Perfect for everyone without conditions
Unpleasant with no helpful response
Acceptable with a room choice to consider
Too expensive for any short trip
questions.explanation: Volvería, pero solicitaría una ubicación concreta; no menciona precio.
questions.evidence: I would stay again for a short work trip, but I would request a back room when booking.

questions.prompt: Who should check local events before booking?
options: Travellers who always miss breakfast
Travellers attending any online course
Travellers who prefer small rooms
Travellers who need quiet every evening
questions.explanation: La recomendación especifica ese tipo de necesidad.
questions.evidence: Travellers who need silence every evening should ask about local events before they decide.

units.title: Un experimento con reuniones
units.objective: Identificar contraste entre eficiencia y acceso a información.
units.strategy: Distingue el dato observado de una conclusión total. Although y however suelen limitar una idea.
units.passage: A design team replaced its daily video meeting with a written update for four weeks. Most staff welcomed the change because they could begin focused work earlier. However, two new colleagues said that the short updates assumed knowledge they did not yet have. The manager had expected fewer meetings to help everyone equally. Instead of returning to daily calls, she introduced a weekly discussion for questions and asked writers to explain unfamiliar terms. The team will review the arrangement next month. So far, the experiment suggests that saving time is useful only if people can still get the information they need.

questions.prompt: Who reported a problem with the written updates?
options: All experienced staff
The entire management team
Two new colleagues
The clients
questions.explanation: El problema no se atribuye a todo el equipo.
questions.evidence: two new colleagues said that the short updates assumed knowledge they did not yet have.

questions.prompt: Why did the manager add a weekly discussion?
options: To replace all written communication
To give experienced staff more reports
To end the experiment immediately
To address information gaps without restoring daily calls
questions.explanation: Conserva el cambio y añade un espacio para preguntas.
questions.evidence: Instead of returning to daily calls, she introduced a weekly discussion for questions

questions.prompt: What is the main lesson so far?
options: Efficiency should not prevent access to necessary information
All meetings waste time
Written messages work equally well for everyone
New colleagues should avoid asking questions
questions.explanation: La conclusión final equilibra ahorro de tiempo e información.
questions.evidence: saving time is useful only if people can still get the information they need.

units.title: Aprender a reparar
units.objective: Inferir propósito a partir de acciones y normas.
units.strategy: Para inferir, combina dos detalles. No añadas motivos que el texto no aporta.
units.passage: At the monthly repair cafe, visitors bring broken household objects and work alongside volunteers. The organisers make clear that this is not a free repair shop: owners stay, ask questions and try simple tasks themselves. Last month, a visitor expected to leave her lamp and return later. After the rule was explained, she stayed and learned how to identify a loose connection. Not every object can be repaired during a session, and volunteers sometimes recommend a qualified specialist. The organisers still consider such visits useful when people leave with a clearer understanding of the problem and a safer plan for dealing with it.

questions.prompt: What are owners expected to do?
options: Leave objects at the door
Repair every object alone
Pay for a new lamp
Stay and participate
questions.explanation: El papel de los propietarios es activo.
questions.evidence: owners stay, ask questions and try simple tasks themselves.

questions.prompt: Why might an unrepaired object still lead to a useful visit?
options: Its owner may understand the problem and next steps better
The object will automatically repair itself
Every owner receives a replacement
Volunteers guarantee a later repair
questions.explanation: Éxito incluye comprensión y un plan seguro, no sólo reparación.
questions.evidence: people leave with a clearer understanding of the problem and a safer plan for dealing with it.

questions.prompt: What does the lamp visitor’s experience illustrate?
options: Visitors can always collect repairs later
The cafe values learning through participation
Only lamps are accepted
Professional help is never needed
questions.explanation: Se quedó y aprendió tras aclararse la norma.
questions.evidence: she stayed and learned how to identify a loose connection.

units.title: Qué significa una consulta pública
units.objective: Evaluar representatividad y distinguir preferencia de necesidad.
units.strategy: Busca quién respondió y quién pudo quedar fuera. Un número no describe por sí solo a toda la comunidad.
units.passage: The council asked residents whether the library should close an hour later on weekdays. Seventy per cent of the online respondents supported the proposal, and an early report described it as the community's clear preference. A librarian noted, however, that most replies came from people who already used the library website. Staff then collected paper responses at a local bus stop and a community centre. These respondents were more concerned about weekend opening and transport home than an extra weekday hour. The council has not rejected the original proposal, but it will compare the needs of different groups before choosing a timetable. The revised report calls the online results valuable but incomplete.

questions.prompt: What limitation did the librarian identify?
options: Online replies mostly came from existing website users
The same users had submitted repeated replies
The online form had emphasised transport rather than opening hours
The responses mainly represented people living near the bus stop
questions.explanation: La muestra inicial favorecía a usuarios del sitio.
questions.evidence: most replies came from people who already used the library website.

questions.prompt: What is the council now planning to do?
options: Give weekend hours priority before comparing other needs
Compare different groups’ needs before deciding
Repeat the online survey with the same website audience
Introduce the weekday extension while studying transport later
questions.explanation: No descarta la propuesta; amplía la base para decidir.
questions.evidence: it will compare the needs of different groups before choosing a timetable.

questions.prompt: What changed between the early and revised reports?
options: The number of extra weekday hours being considered
The method used to count support within the online sample
The strength of the claim about the whole community
The willingness of website users to answer another survey
questions.explanation: Pasa de preferencia clara de toda la comunidad a resultados incompletos.
questions.evidence: The revised report calls the online results valuable but incomplete.

units.title: Resultados con matices
units.objective: Distinguir reducción de material y resultado ambiental global.

vocabulary.example: The bag has a reinforced base.
Do not judge solely by price.

units.strategy: Localiza la medida usada. No confundas mejorar una variable con mejorar todas.
units.passage: A food delivery company tested lighter packaging on one route. The new boxes used less cardboard, and the company initially presented this as an environmental improvement. During the trial, however, more meals arrived damaged and had to be replaced. The operations team pointed out that extra journeys and wasted food also mattered. It would therefore be premature to judge the packaging solely by its weight. The company is testing a reinforced corner rather than abandoning the lighter design completely. It will count damaged deliveries as well as material use in the next trial. The aim is to reduce waste across the delivery process, not merely to make each empty box lighter.

questions.prompt: What unexpected problem occurred?
options: Replacement meals required a different cardboard supplier
More meals arrived damaged
The lighter boxes took longer to assemble
The meals needed more time to cool before delivery
questions.explanation: El aumento de daños obligó a reponer pedidos.
questions.evidence: more meals arrived damaged and had to be replaced.

questions.prompt: Why is packaging weight alone insufficient?
options: Box weight varies too much between routes to compare
Customers’ packaging preferences affect their repeat orders
Damage can cause extra journeys and wasted food
The empty boxes also take up space in delivery vehicles
questions.explanation: La medida aislada omite efectos en otras etapas.
questions.evidence: extra journeys and wasted food also mattered.

questions.prompt: What best describes the company’s next step?
options: Retest the unchanged design using a longer delivery route
Restore the original boxes while measuring material use
Reinforce the whole box and compare only replacement costs
Modify the design and assess broader effects
questions.explanation: Refuerza esquinas y añade daños a las medidas, sin desechar toda la idea.
questions.evidence: It will count damaged deliveries as well as material use in the next trial.

units.title: La neutralidad de una etiqueta
units.objective: Interpretar punto de vista y función de una objeción.
units.strategy: Separa lo que sostiene una persona de lo que el texto presenta como hecho. Revisa a quién se atribuye cada opinión.
units.passage: When a museum rewrote its labels in plain language, visitor feedback became more positive. Some curators nevertheless worried that shorter descriptions might hide uncertainty about where objects came from. One label, for example, described an item as a gift although records did not establish whether its owner had freely agreed to the transfer. The writing team argued that accessibility need not require a confident answer where none existed. It revised the label to state what was known and what remained disputed. The debate was not simply about choosing easy words. It concerned whether clarity meant removing complexity or helping visitors recognise it. The museum now tests labels for both readability and the accuracy of their qualifications.

questions.prompt: Why was the word “gift” questioned?
options: The records disagreed about which year the transfer occurred
The label failed to explain who had received the item
Consent to the transfer had not been established
The term concealed a disagreement about the object’s monetary value
questions.explanation: Gift sugería consentimiento voluntario que los registros no confirmaban.
questions.evidence: records did not establish whether its owner had freely agreed to the transfer.

questions.prompt: What does the writing team’s response suggest?
options: Readability should be assessed before historical accuracy
Disputed information is better explained outside the main label
More specialist vocabulary would solve the uncertainty
Plain language can communicate uncertainty
questions.explanation: La revisión declara lo conocido y lo discutido con claridad.
questions.evidence: It revised the label to state what was known and what remained disputed.

questions.prompt: What is the central issue in the debate?
options: How to be clear without erasing complexity
How to balance visitor preferences against shorter viewing times
Whether incomplete records justify removing an object from display
How to describe the transfer without referring to the owner
questions.explanation: El texto formula explícitamente las dos interpretaciones de claridad.
questions.evidence: whether clarity meant removing complexity or helping visitors recognise it.

units.title: Igualdad en una convocatoria
units.objective: Reconocer supuestos e inferir efecto de una regla.

vocabulary.example: Two teams withdrew from the event.
Use an example to demonstrate the idea.

units.strategy: Una regla idéntica puede tener efectos distintos. Busca las condiciones que el argumento da por supuestas.
units.passage: A small arts fund required applicants to submit professionally edited videos. The panel believed this would make proposals easier to compare. Yet several community groups withdrew, explaining that hiring an editor would consume much of the funding they hoped to receive. The same requirement applied to everyone, but the resources available to meet it were unequal. After reviewing the withdrawals, the fund accepted a simple recorded presentation or a written proposal with images. Assessors continued to use the same artistic criteria. The revision did not lower the stated standard of the work; it changed how applicants could demonstrate that standard. Whether the new process reaches more groups will be checked after the next application round.

questions.prompt: Why did several groups withdraw?
options: The short application deadline prevented them finding an editor
The panel required videos longer than their available material
The grant excluded the cost of producing the artwork itself
Professional editing would use too much of the hoped-for funding
questions.explanation: La barrera era el coste del formato exigido.
questions.evidence: hiring an editor would consume much of the funding they hoped to receive.

questions.prompt: What remained unchanged after the revision?
options: The artistic assessment criteria
The range of presentation formats accepted
The need to employ a professional editor
The amount groups would need to spend on professional editing
questions.explanation: Se flexibiliza la evidencia admitida, no el criterio artístico.
questions.evidence: Assessors continued to use the same artistic criteria.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is justified at this stage?
options: The new formats have already attracted previously excluded groups
The process has changed, but wider participation is not yet confirmed
The revision changes both the entry format and artistic standards
The fund now knows that editing costs were the only participation barrier
questions.explanation: La comprobación de alcance está prevista para después.
questions.evidence: Whether the new process reaches more groups will be checked after the next application round.

units.title: Una cifra que oculta trabajo
units.objective: Analizar una medida de rendimiento y una concesión argumentativa.

vocabulary.example: A subsequent review found an error.
We are working towards a resolution.

units.strategy: Identifica qué cuenta la métrica y qué deja fuera. Una concesión reconoce un beneficio sin aceptar toda la conclusión.
units.passage: A support department celebrated a sharp fall in the time needed to close customer requests after introducing an automated reply system. On paper, the change looked decisive. A subsequent review found that some requests were marked closed as soon as a standard message was sent, even when customers needed further help. Those customers often opened a new request, which appeared as a separate case. The reviewer did not argue that automation had no value: routine questions were being answered more quickly. Her objection was to treating closure speed as a sufficient measure of resolution. She recommended tracking whether customers had to make contact again and asking a sample of them whether their problem was solved. A faster administrative action, she observed, was not necessarily a faster service.

questions.prompt: Why could one unresolved problem appear as separate cases?
options: Customers opened new requests after automatic closure
Staff divided longer requests into separate questions before replying
The review grouped requests according to the department receiving them
Standard replies were counted once when sent and again when read
questions.explanation: Una nueva solicitud se contaba como caso separado aunque persistiera el problema.
questions.evidence: Those customers often opened a new request, which appeared as a separate case.

questions.prompt: What benefit does the reviewer acknowledge?
options: Fewer customers needed to reopen complex cases
Routine questions were answered faster
Staff spent less time reviewing dissatisfied customers’ messages
The measure distinguished simple questions from difficult ones
questions.explanation: Es la concesión explícita; su crítica no niega toda utilidad.
questions.evidence: routine questions were being answered more quickly.

questions.prompt: What does the final sentence challenge?
options: Assuming repeat contact indicates a failure in the automatic reply
Comparing automated replies with messages written by staff
Equating administrative speed with effective service
Treating customer satisfaction as more useful than resolution data
questions.explanation: Distingue cerrar un expediente de resolver una necesidad.
questions.evidence: A faster administrative action, she observed, was not necessarily a faster service.

units.title: La voz del traductor
units.objective: Interpretar límites de una explicación y una elección editorial.

vocabulary.example: He conceded that the task was difficult.

units.strategy: Pregunta qué se conserva y qué se pierde. No conviertas una preferencia del autor en regla universal.
units.passage: Reviewing a translated novel, a critic praised its fluent dialogue but questioned the decision to replace every regional expression with a neutral equivalent. The translator replied that unfamiliar phrases could interrupt the story for readers with no knowledge of the setting. This was a reasonable concern, the critic conceded, yet removing all such friction also made characters from different generations sound remarkably alike. She did not propose retaining every original phrase or filling each page with notes. Rather, she suggested preserving selected differences whose significance could emerge from context. Her complaint was therefore not that the translation was too easy to read, but that one kind of ease had been purchased at the expense of distinctions central to the novel's social world.

questions.prompt: Why did the translator use neutral equivalents?
options: To distinguish older speakers from younger readers
To avoid interrupting readers unfamiliar with the setting
To make the setting less specific to one region
To compensate for missing explanatory notes in the original
questions.explanation: Esa es la justificación atribuida al traductor, no una intención de borrar edades.
questions.evidence: unfamiliar phrases could interrupt the story for readers with no knowledge of the setting.

questions.prompt: Which alternative does the critic favour?
options: Retaining regional differences and explaining each in a footnote
Neutralising unfamiliar phrases while describing characters’ ages elsewhere
Keeping selected differences understandable through context
Preserving expressions only when an exact neutral equivalent is available
questions.explanation: La propuesta es selectiva y contextual.
questions.evidence: preserving selected differences whose significance could emerge from context.

questions.prompt: What is the critic’s main objection?
options: The translation preserves regional differences but makes them hard to infer
The use of notes interrupts dialogue more than unfamiliar language would
Neutral wording has made the plot’s sequence of events harder to follow
Uniform ease has weakened meaningful social differences
questions.explanation: Critica el coste de una estrategia uniforme, no la legibilidad en sí.
questions.evidence: one kind of ease had been purchased at the expense of distinctions central to the novel's social world.

units.title: Evidencia y decisión pública
units.objective: Evaluar una afirmación causal y el alcance de una recomendación.

vocabulary.example: The observation period lasted a month.
He was not indifferent to their concerns.

units.strategy: Distingue después de de a causa de. Examina qué comparación falta antes de aceptar una explicación causal.
units.passage: After a town introduced free evening parking, restaurant bookings rose. A business association cited the increase as proof that the policy had revived the centre. The council's analyst was less categorical. A new theatre programme had begun during the same period, and bookings had also increased in a nearby town where parking charges were unchanged. These observations did not establish that free parking had no effect; they weakened the claim that it alone explained the rise. The analyst recommended extending the observation period and comparing similar locations before making the policy permanent. Critics called this unnecessary hesitation. In her response, she distinguished postponing a final judgement from refusing to act: the temporary scheme could continue while its contribution was investigated. Her position was cautious about attribution, not indifferent to the town's businesses.

questions.prompt: Which observation challenges the claim that free parking alone caused the rise?
options: The parking scheme had initially been introduced as a temporary measure
Restaurant owners supported the parking scheme after bookings rose
Bookings rose in a nearby town without a parking-price change
The council collected bookings data over a temporary observation period
questions.explanation: Hay un incremento comparable sin esa intervención; esto cuestiona exclusividad, no demuestra efecto nulo.
questions.evidence: bookings had also increased in a nearby town where parking charges were unchanged.

questions.prompt: What does the analyst propose during further investigation?
options: Suspend the scheme until a comparison has been completed
Confirm the policy while postponing judgement on the theatre’s contribution
Extend free parking to neighbouring towns to create comparison sites
Allow the temporary scheme to continue
questions.explanation: Separa continuar una medida provisional de emitir un juicio definitivo.
questions.evidence: the temporary scheme could continue while its contribution was investigated.

questions.prompt: Which statement most accurately represents her position?
options: A beneficial effect is possible, but the causal claim is overstated
The available comparison shows that the scheme is probably ineffective
A permanent policy is justified because uncertainty cannot be eliminated
The theatre programme is a stronger established explanation than parking
questions.explanation: El texto niega que los datos prueben efecto nulo y cuestiona la explicación exclusiva.
questions.evidence: These observations did not establish that free parking had no effect; they weakened the claim that it alone explained the rise.

units.title: Lo que no conserva un archivo
units.objective: Interpretar una metáfora, un matiz y un límite de conocimiento.

vocabulary.example: The report presents a seamless story.

units.strategy: Distingue ausencia de evidencia y evidencia de ausencia. Busca la propuesta que evita ambos extremos.
units.passage: An exhibition promised to tell the complete history of a coastal district through its surviving letters. The archive was rich, but most of the letters had been written by property owners; seasonal workers appeared mainly when someone complained about them. A historian welcomed the exhibition while questioning its promise of completeness. Silence in an archive, she argued, is not a transparent window onto an uneventful life. It may reveal whose words were considered worth preserving. Nor did she suggest that missing voices could simply be invented. She proposed displaying the gaps alongside the letters and combining them with carefully attributed oral accounts. The resulting exhibition would offer a less seamless story, but a more honest account of how that story had been assembled. Acknowledging the limits of the evidence would become part of the explanation rather than an embarrassment to conceal.

questions.prompt: Why are the letters a limited basis for a complete history?
options: They report complaints without recording the museum’s response
They were selected to support oral accounts collected for the exhibition
They provide more detail about seasonal employment than about property
They mostly represent property owners’ voices
questions.explanation: Los trabajadores aparecen a través de quejas ajenas, no con representación equivalente.
questions.evidence: most of the letters had been written by property owners; seasonal workers appeared mainly when someone complained about them.

questions.prompt: What does the “transparent window” image warn against?
options: Assuming missing records mean that little happened
Assuming oral accounts offer a clearer picture than written evidence
Treating complaints as reliable descriptions of particular workers
Interpreting property ownership as the main cause of archival loss
questions.explanation: La metáfora cuestiona tratar silencio documental como descripción completa de una vida.
questions.evidence: Silence in an archive, she argued, is not a transparent window onto an uneventful life.

questions.prompt: What approach does the historian recommend?
options: Reconstruct workers’ likely experiences to complete the written record
Make evidence gaps visible and add sourced oral accounts
Prioritise oral accounts and reserve letters for corroborating details
Present the surviving letters together without discussing their selection
questions.explanation: La alternativa reconoce límites sin fabricar testimonios.
questions.evidence: She proposed displaying the gaps alongside the letters and combining them with carefully attributed oral accounts.
